clue.text: When power's gone, want to break up fight

indicators.note: the word for want is set to break up the word for fight by sitting inside it

parts.note: a bout is a fight or contest, as in boxing
want means lack, a shortage

explanation.surface: During a power cut someone is keen to stop a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackout is a period when the electricity supply fails, so power is gone.

clue.text: This is turned out of paella, theoretically

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words paella theoretically

explanation.surface: Something is supposedly flipped out of a pan of paella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This is turned' reads as 'this is what things are turned on', the woodworker's sense of turning.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine on which wood or metal is turned to shape it.

indicators.note: abusing mistreats the words, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A junkie misuses heroin, also called smack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abusing' rearranges HEROIN SMACK; the smoker is the addict, not the heroin user the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain-smoker lights one cigarette from another, addicted to nicotine.

definitions.meaning: in music a turn is a decorative figure of notes, a kind of embellishment
to adorn or decorate something

explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is a musical embellishment such as a turn, and to ornament is to decorate.

clue.text: Don't be knocked out by blow to the face?

definitions.text: Don't be knocked out by blow to the face?

parts.words: Don't be knocked out by blow to the face?
parts.note: a boxer who absorbs a punch to the jaw without going down; figuratively, accept a setback bravely

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to endure misfortune stoically, literally to absorb a punch on the jaw.

clue.text: Number at sea close to mutiny after cry of insubordination

indicators.note: the close of mutiny is placed after the cry, so it comes later in the word

parts.note: shan't! is a defiant refusal to obey

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here taken from mutiny

explanation.surface: A sailor on the brink of mutiny shouts a refusal to his captain.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a song sung by sailors at work, and a number is a song.

definitions.meaning: a conifer of the genus Picea
neat, smart and trim

explanation.definitionFit: Spruce is a coniferous tree and an adjective meaning smart and neat.

clue.text: Tree from which money doesn't originate

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter, which is missing here

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: A tree from which money does not grow.
explanation.walkthrough: It plays on the saying that money doesn't grow on trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The ash is a common deciduous tree.

clue.text: Fixed rate more stable for fund manager

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of repaired or rearranged, so the letters of rate are reordered

parts.note: surer means steadier, more stable

explanation.surface: A fixed interest rate offers more security to an investor.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer looks after the funds of an organisation.

definitions.meaning: a tune or passage of music, something set down in notes
an injury to a muscle from overstretching

explanation.definitionFit: Strain means both a musical melody and a pulled-muscle injury, the two senses here.

clue.text: Royals head for material over crown

parts.note: K is king and ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen: two royals
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth
a chief is a head or leader

explanation.surface: The royal family's leader chooses fabric to drape over the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royals' gives two pieces, K for king and ER for the queen, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerchief is a square of cloth worn over the head, and the crown is the top of the head.

definitions.meaning: to tend towards something is to incline or ... that way
thin, without much fat

explanation.definitionFit: Lean is a verb meaning incline or tend, and an adjective meaning thin.

definitions.meaning: a ... can be a principal route sailed by ships
the main dish of a meal comes after the starter, so it is not a starter

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the main dish of a meal and, nautically, a principal sailing route.

clue.text: Two girls holding one rope, not initially tied up

parts.note: Una and Val are girls' names

indicators.note: the second girl holds the numeral inside her name

parts.note: Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word for rope loses its initial letter

parts.note: a cable is a thick rope

explanation.surface: A pair of girls grip a rope, but it isn't tied up at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' takes C off CABLE, leaving ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tied up is busy and so unavailable.

parts.note: damn and flaming are both mild British expletives used as intensifiers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flaming' is a mild British swear word, like 'damn' or 'bloody'.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a tall pink wading bird.

clue.text: Dog licks round horse lil a duck!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Dog licks round horse lil a duck!', garbled by OCR and cut off on the scan; the wordplay (perhaps LAPS round HAS A, plus O) cannot be confirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: Dog licks round horse lil a duck!

clue.text: Open milk products, taking top off

indicators.note: removing the top of a down-style word means losing its first letter

parts.note: dairy means milk, butter, cheese and the like

explanation.surface: Someone opens dairy goods by removing the lids.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy means open, spacious and well ventilated.

clue.text: Pack some of it for seaman

parts.note: a deck is a pack of cards
a hand is the share of the pack dealt to one player

explanation.surface: Someone takes part of a pack of cards to sew a seam.
explanation.walkthrough: The hand is the part of the deck held by one player.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is a sailor who works on deck, an ordinary seaman.

definitions.meaning: to second a proposal is to support or ... it
years ... means years ago, in the past

explanation.definitionFit: Back means to support (second) as a verb and in the past (ago) as an adverb.

indicators.note: confusing the words mixes their letters into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A writer complains that some sources are muddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' rearranges ARE THUS into THESAUR; I for 'one' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesauri are reference books of synonyms, the plural of thesaurus.

definitions.meaning: a shoemaker works at his last, the foot-shaped block
eventually, after a long time

explanation.definitionFit: At last means finally, and a cobbler is at his last, the shoe form he works on.

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it
to streak is to move very fast, and a streak is such a dash

explanation.surface: A butterfly flits about in startled haste.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairstreaks are a group of small butterflies with fine streaks on their wings.

definitions.meaning: a small green sour citrus fruit
quicklime, calcium oxide, is a strongly alkaline substance

explanation.definitionFit: Lime names both a sour citrus fruit and quicklime, an alkaline chemical used in building.

clue.text: Edible fungus — second helping on to plate of student?

parts.note: asking for more means a second helping
learner drivers in Britain show an L-plate

explanation.surface: A student is served a second portion of food on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: An L-plate is the red L sign displayed by a learner driver in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The morel is a prized edible mushroom with a honeycombed cap.

definitions.meaning: to ... a task is to start tackling it
a way of dealing with something, a stance or attitude

explanation.definitionFit: Approach as a verb means begin tackling something; as a noun it means a manner or stance.

definitions.meaning: old British slang for strange or peculiar
an alcoholic drink, here the spirit made from sugar cane

explanation.definitionFit: Rum means strange in British slang and is a spirit distilled from sugar cane.

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a burn is a small stream, chiefly in Scotland

explanation.surface: A sunlit brook runs through shady woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: BURN is a Scottish and northern English word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn is a reddish-brown colour, and a shade is a colour.

indicators.note: the keep hides the mother inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a keep is a castle's stronghold, a fort
ma is mother; the possessive s gives no letter

explanation.surface: A secret kept by someone's mother has been arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A format is the layout or arrangement of something.

clue.text: Outlaw journalist, hack finally trapped by girl

indicators.note: the girl's name surrounds the other pieces, holding them captive inside

parts.note: Nelly is a girl's name
ED is short for editor, a journalist

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of hack

explanation.surface: A reporter, a hack at heart, ends up cornered by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Ned Kelly was a famous nineteenth-century Australian bushranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Ned Kelly is the best-known Australian bushranger, a celebrated outlaw.
